chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Nahdi, from his father, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'If there were not in the earth except two, the Imam would be one of the two.'

key_terms.الأرض: The earth — used here to indicate the totality of human existence; the hadith implies the earth cannot be without an Imam
key_terms.الإمام: The Imam — the divinely appointed guide and authority; in Shia theology, the infallible successor to the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Does Shia Islam teach that the earth is never without an Imam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the universal and perpetual necessity of the Imam (divine guide) — that even if the entire population of the earth were reduced to only two people, one of them would still be the Imam. This hadith establishes the Shia doctrine that the earth is never without a hujja (proof/authority of God), and that the Imamate is not a contingent social institution but a metaphysical necessity embedded in God's design for creation. The early Shia audience would have understood this as a refutation of those who denied the necessity of the Imam after the Prophet.
